## Symptom
CI-only flake in `tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py::test_fixture_batched_map_recovers_from_one_transient_git_read[rc128]`. Observed on Gerrit change 1837 ps3 (GH run 32032700192, ubuntu py3.12, xdist worker popen-gw1):

    assert batched[position] == authorship.resolve_event_commit(position, ticket_dir)
    E  AssertionError: assert 'c7c2f6...' == None
    E   where None = resolve_event_commit('1002-bbbb1111', '.../aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd')

## Root cause
The equivalence assertion compares two resolvers over the same fixture git history:
- batched side (`_fixture_batched_map` -> `build_ticket_position_commit_map`) is wrapped in a 5-attempt transient-recovery loop in the test.
- oracle side (`src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py::resolve_event_commit`) is documented fail-closed: 'Any failure - git non-zero, no match, git missing, a timeout, or any exception - yields None; this function NEVER raises.' It has NO transient retry.

When a transient git object-store read hits the *oracle* call in CI, it returns None while the batched side has already recovered, so the assertion fails. This is exactly the git-read-transient class the file's own forensics/transient infra (bugs innovative-dandruffy-deer, warmthless-dermal-oropendola) was built to diagnose - but only the batched side was hardened.

## Evidence it is environmental / not a code regression
- Deterministically PASSES locally: 5/5 in isolation, 12/12 x3 under xdist -n auto.
- Unrelated to the change it surfaced on (RP-01 S4 = LLM structured-output tracing; this is the authorship subsystem).
- S1-S3 of the same stack passed this test at Verified+1.

## Fix direction (not done here)
Wrap the oracle side of the equivalence assertion in the same bounded transient-retry the batched side uses (or give `resolve_event_commit` an internal bounded retry for transient rc!=0/OSError, keeping the fail-closed contract for a genuine no-match). Do NOT retry-until-green in CI.
